title: Breadth-First Search
description: Explores an unweighted graph one layer at a time. It returns the fewest-edge path when every move has the same cost.
observe: The frontier spreads evenly outward from the start, even when the goal lies in one direction.
tradeoff: Simple and complete on finite graphs, but it ignores goal direction and edge costs.

title: Depth-First Search
description: Follows one branch as far as it can before backing up. It is useful for reachability, but it does not generally find a shortest path.
observe: One narrow tendril dives through the maze before nearby alternatives are explored.
tradeoff: Uses a compact frontier; its route quality can vary sharply with neighbor order.

title: Greedy Best-First
description: Ranks frontier nodes by estimated distance to the goal. It is an eager goal seeker that may overlook the cost already paid.
observe: The search leans toward the goal and can get caught exploring the wrong side of an obstacle.
tradeoff: Often reaches a goal quickly, with no general shortest-path guarantee.

title: A*
description: Balances the route cost already paid with a lower-bound estimate of the remaining cost. With a suitable admissible heuristic, it can find an optimal path.
observe: The frontier follows a corridor between the start-cost wave and the goal estimate.
tradeoff: A useful heuristic can reduce search; memory use can grow with the explored frontier.

title: Bidirectional Dijkstra
description: Runs Dijkstra search from both endpoints and joins the two explored regions. It requires an exact goal node.
observe: Two waves move toward one another and meet before either crosses the entire map.
tradeoff: Can reduce explored distance on suitable graphs; maintains two search states.

title: Bidirectional A*
description: Searches from both endpoints with potential-reweighted edges. The supported contract requires a consistent heuristic and an exact goal.
observe: Two guided frontiers advance toward a meeting point rather than searching from only one end.
tradeoff: Benefits depend on the heuristic and graph; consistency is part of the correctness contract.

title: Dijkstra
description: Expands the currently cheapest known route without a goal-directed heuristic. It finds shortest paths with non-negative edge costs.
observe: A cost wave expands in every direction, reaching nearby cheap cells first.
tradeoff: Reliable with non-negative costs, though it may explore far beyond the useful corridor.

title: D* Lite
description: Reuses search information when edge costs change on a stable graph topology. The planner can move its start and update directed edges between queries.
observe: After an obstacle appears, the route is repaired around the changed region.
tradeoff: Useful for repeated replanning; topology changes require a new planner session.

title: Weighted A*
description: Gives the goal estimate extra weight so the search can focus more aggressively. Path quality depends on the chosen weight and stopping condition.
observe: The frontier narrows toward the goal, sometimes accepting a longer detour around a wall.
tradeoff: Can reach a feasible route sooner, trading away ordinary A* optimality.

title: Re-expansion A*
description: Uses Weighted A* with conditional reopening of closed nodes when a better route is discovered. Reopening behavior is controlled by the configured threshold mode.
observe: A previously settled node can re-enter the search when a sufficiently better route arrives.
tradeoff: Adds recovery from inconsistent ordering; more re-expansions can mean more work.

title: Anytime A*
principle: find a route, then improve it
description: Runs a sequence of weighted A* searches and keeps the best solution found. Each pass has its own expansion budget; the returned result reports the final incumbent.
observe: A usable path appears first, then later passes try to shorten it.
tradeoff: Can provide an early feasible path; total work spans multiple search passes.

title: Jump Point Search
description: Skips symmetric intermediate expansions on uniform-cost 2D grids while retaining jump points. Returned paths still include every traversed cell.
observe: Long straight stretches collapse into a few meaningful turning points.
tradeoff: Specialized for the standard uniform 8-connected grid and its corner rule.

title: Weighted Jump Point Search
description: Applies jump-point reasoning to a positive-cost terrain grid. Moves account for the terrain values they cross; diagonal corner cutting is forbidden.
observe: The route bends around costly terrain as well as blocked cells.
tradeoff: Requires a terrain grid with valid positive costs; not interchangeable with uniform JPS.

title: Theta*
description: Extends grid search with visible parent shortcuts, producing any-angle paths between grid waypoints. Every segment is checked against obstacles.
observe: The route cuts visible corners instead of turning at every grid cell.
tradeoff: Optimizes a different path space from octile-optimal grid paths.

title: Lazy Theta*
description: Considers candidate any-angle parent shortcuts optimistically, then checks visibility when a node is expanded and repairs blocked shortcuts.
observe: A promising shortcut appears first; blocked line segments are checked and replaced later.
tradeoff: Can defer visibility checks; candidate paths must still be validated.

title: RRT
description: Grows a tree from the start by sampling free-space targets and extending toward them. It is designed to find a feasible route in continuous spaces.
observe: Branches grow toward scattered samples while obstacle-crossing motions are rejected.
tradeoff: Good at finding feasible paths in broad spaces; paths are not generally optimal.

title: RRT*
description: Adds neighborhood rewiring to RRT so new states can improve nearby parent choices. Its asymptotic behavior depends on the sampling and neighborhood conditions.
observe: The tree changes its local connections after new samples arrive.
tradeoff: Extra neighbor checks can improve path quality over time but add computation.

title: Informed RRT*
description: After finding a solution, focuses new samples inside a region that could improve the current path, under the supported Euclidean path-length objective.
observe: Once a first route exists, sampling concentrates in an ellipse around promising paths.
tradeoff: Informed bounds depend on an exact point goal and additive Euclidean path length.

title: FMT*
description: Plans through a fixed random sample set using a lazy dynamic-programming wavefront. In this project, sample_count defines that fixed set.
observe: A connected wavefront moves across samples instead of adding a new sample at every step.
tradeoff: The fixed batch limits the candidate set for that planning call.

title: PRM*
description: Builds a reusable random geometric roadmap, then connects exact query endpoints and searches the graph. Local motions are checked for validity.
observe: Free samples are joined into a roadmap, then a route is traced through it.
tradeoff: Roadmap construction can be reused across queries; sample count and connection radius matter.

title: Lazy PRM
description: Builds a roadmap with unvalidated candidate edges. It checks only edges on a candidate route, removes blocked ones and searches again.
observe: Only the current best-looking route is collision-checked; a blocked edge triggers another route search.
tradeoff: Can avoid checking many unused edges; validation and cache state affect later queries.

title: AIT*
description: Uses a reverse search over a finite sampled graph to estimate cost-to-go, then prioritizes forward edge checks. This implementation does not claim the paper's asymptotic-optimality guarantee.
observe: A goal-side estimate guides which start-side edge is checked next.
tradeoff: The current implementation uses a finite sample graph and recomputes reverse shortest paths after blocked edges.

title: EIT*
description: Adds estimated collision-check effort to an asymmetric reverse/forward search. The current implementation uses a fixed sample graph and does not claim the paper's asymptotic-optimality guarantee.
observe: Edges expected to be easier to validate are preferred among similarly promising choices.
tradeoff: Collision effort is an estimate; this implementation omits some reference-algorithm features.

title: EIRM*
description: Keeps a sampled roadmap and caches valid or blocked edges for repeated exact start/goal queries in a caller-managed world version.
observe: Later queries can reuse roadmap edges whose validity is already known.
tradeoff: World changes must advance the version or reset the roadmap to avoid stale validity.

title: FCIT*
description: Orders useful outgoing edges from reached samples in a fully connected sampled graph and restarts over new informed batches while retaining the valid tree.
observe: An edge queue narrows toward connections that could improve the current path.
tradeoff: A fully connected batch can create many candidate edges.

title: RIT*
description: Uses a positive-definite metric tensor to price motion and shape sampling or connection neighborhoods for additive Riemannian arc length.
observe: The search region stretches along directions that are cheaper under the local metric.
tradeoff: Metric bounds and tensor validity are part of the planning contract.

title: JIT*
description: Uses collision feedback to focus later samples near failed edges, while retaining nonzero uniform sampling. Its objective can include manipulability.
observe: A failed motion seeds a focused sampling corridor; exploration still extends beyond it.
tradeoff: The manipulability objective requires a compatible robot Jacobian.

title: Hybrid A*
description: Searches continuous SE(2) poses grouped by discretized position, heading and gear, using curvature-bounded vehicle motions with footprint checks.
observe: The vehicle turns through feasible arcs instead of sliding sideways between grid cells.
tradeoff: Motion primitives and collision sampling must match the vehicle geometry.

title: State Lattice
description: Runs A* over discretized SE(2) poses connected by supplied local-frame motion primitives, checking the robot footprint along each motion.
observe: The reachable pose graph is built from physically shaped local moves.
tradeoff: The primitive set determines which motions are representable.

title: BIT*
description: Connects batches of samples through an ordered edge search and focuses later batches using the best known solution, under additive Euclidean path length.
observe: New sample batches appear, then the edge queue prioritizes the most promising connections.
tradeoff: The exact point-goal, metric and objective restrictions matter for its bounds.

title: ABIT*
description: Runs informed batch searches with progressively refined search effort and keeps an incumbent solution. It shares the supported additive path-length restrictions.
observe: A feasible route is retained while later search passes refine the candidate set.
tradeoff: Solution quality and work depend on the search schedule and stopping budget.

title: RRT-Connect
description: Grows trees from both start and goal and repeatedly tries to connect them through free space.
observe: Two branches approach one another until they form a continuous route.
tradeoff: Often finds feasible paths quickly; it does not generally optimize path length.

title: SIPP
description: Plans through a graph whose nodes and edges have blocked time intervals. The agent can wait while its current node remains safe.
observe: The route waits at a safe location, then crosses when the next time window opens.
tradeoff: Requires known positive durations and half-open blocked intervals.

title: Bounded-Suboptimal SIPP
description: Keeps states within a weight-bounded band of the best lower-bound estimate and chooses among them by remaining graph distance.
observe: A slightly later but simpler safe schedule may be selected from the focal band.
tradeoff: The suboptimality bound holds only when the search finishes successfully.

title: Kinodynamic SIPP
description: Propagates arrival-time intervals through speed-labeled configurations using constant-acceleration motion primitives.
observe: The agent must slow to zero before it can wait; a moving robot cannot pause instantly.
tradeoff: Requires integer time ticks and finite speed, acceleration and deceleration limits.

title: EECBS
description: Plans for multiple agents with conflict-based search, explicit estimation for high-level node selection and focal A* for each constrained path.
observe: A detected collision branches into constraints that redirect one agent at a time.
tradeoff: The suboptimality guarantee depends on the weight and successful termination.

title: LaCAM*
description: Builds collision-free joint moves lazily by assigning one agent's next location at a time and rejecting partial assignments with conflicts.
observe: Agents negotiate a shared next configuration rather than planning independent paths only.
tradeoff: Uses unit-weight undirected graphs; agents remain at their goals after arrival.
